thesis.line: Physical AI studies how the physical world gets changed in the age of AI.
thesis.body: Changing the world takes two moves. First model it: build a representation faithful enough to act on. Then change it: push a decision into the world through an embodiment — a human wearing glasses, a robot arm, or the two together. Acting changes the world, which changes what has to be modeled, so the two moves close into a loop. Every axis below is a column on that loop. The sections here are filters over those columns rather than folders.

views.name: Modeling the physical world
views.blurb: Build a representation of the world faithful enough to act on. The world is objects and the changes they undergo, so the two questions that separate these papers are which facet of it you represent and in what form you hold it.

groups.name: Objects: identity, state, and change
groups.sub: Objects turn up in almost every group below. These are the papers where the object representation itself is the contribution.

groups.name: Latent predictive world models
groups.sub: Predict the next state in a learned embedding. Skip the pixels that do not matter for acting.

groups.name: Generative world models
groups.sub: The state is a frame and prediction is generation, so the model is also a simulator you can look at.

groups.name: Physics, materials, deformation
groups.sub: Forces, mass, friction, cloth and rope. What happens next without anyone asking.

groups.name: Hands, bodies, and contact
groups.sub: Where a body meets an object: grasp, contact, affordance, human-object interaction.

groups.name: Scenes, 3D and 4D
groups.sub: Geometry and layout — the stage everything else happens on.

groups.name: Egocentric corpora: the raw material
groups.sub: The recordings the human-embodiment half of this field is built out of. Read the collection protocol as closely as the headline hours.

groups.name: Procedure and task structure
groups.sub: Time above the frame: steps, goals, orderings, task graphs. Where a minute of video becomes a plan.

views.name: Changing the physical world
views.blurb: A decision becomes a change in atoms only through an embodiment. Who carries it — a guided person, a robot, or both — decides the channel, the failure modes and the evaluation, which is why the two literatures barely cite each other.

groups.name: Human and robot together
groups.sub: Shared autonomy, teleoperation, handover, mixed-reality interfaces. Both sides touch the same task.

groups.name: Checking the human's work
groups.sub: Did the intended change actually happen? Mistake detection is the verify stage of a human-embodied loop, and the largest cluster on this list.

groups.name: Guiding the human
groups.sub: The person moves the atoms and the system perceives, decides, and tells or shows. Glasses, AR, coaching, task assistants.

groups.name: Human video becomes robot action
groups.sub: Human footage is the cheapest embodiment data there is. These papers turn a person's hands into a policy.

groups.name: Robot as the embodiment
groups.sub: The policy emits torques or waypoints. Vision-language-action models, manipulation, humanoids, planners.

groups.name: Acting without a body yet
groups.sub: The action is a call, a plan or a latent move. Includes the agent loops the embodied ones borrowed from.

views.name: Closing the loop
views.blurb: A cross-section rather than a third topic. These papers consume the effect of their own action at run time, which is where modeling and changing stop being separable. Every paper here already appeared above.

groups.name: Loops closed around a person
groups.sub: Observe, decide, tell the person, watch what they do about it.

groups.name: Loops closed around a robot
groups.sub: Observe, act, check whether the world moved the way the model said it would.

groups.name: Loops with nothing actuated
groups.sub: The loop exists inside the model or inside a simulator.

fields.label: Arc
fields.help: The two moves of physical AI. A paper can do both.

vocab.label: Model the world
vocab.help: Contributes a representation, an understanding, or a prediction of the physical world.

vocab.label: Change the world
vocab.help: Contributes something that moves atoms — a policy, a guidance signal, an intervention.

fields.label: Loop stage
fields.help: Where in perceive → decide → act → check the contribution sits. Multi-select, because most systems span a few.

vocab.label: Sense
vocab.help: Turn sensors into observations.

vocab.label: Represent
vocab.help: Turn observations into a state you can act on.

vocab.label: Anticipate
vocab.help: Predict what the world does next.

vocab.label: Decide
vocab.help: Choose the next step or plan.

vocab.label: Act
vocab.help: Emit the action — motor command, instruction, or overlay.

vocab.label: Verify
vocab.help: Check whether the intended change actually happened.

vocab.label: Adapt
vocab.help: Change the policy or the model from the outcome.

fields.label: Closes the loop
fields.help: The system feeds its own effect back as input at run time. A one-shot predictor does not. A re-planning agent does.

fields.label: Embodiment
fields.help: Who or what actually moves the atoms.

vocab.label: None
vocab.help: Nothing is actuated. The paper models the world or would-be actions without a body.

vocab.label: Human
vocab.help: A person is the actuator; the AI observes and guides. Wearables, AR, coaching.

vocab.label: Robot
vocab.help: Arm, mobile base, humanoid, or dexterous hand.

vocab.label: Human+Robot
vocab.help: Both act on the same physical task — collaboration, handover, teleoperation.

vocab.label: Simulated
vocab.help: The body exists only in simulation.

fields.label: Human role
fields.help: What the human is to the system. Separate from embodiment: a person can be data without being an actuator, and can be both the one guided and the one judging.

vocab.label: Observed
vocab.help: The human is a source of data, not a participant.

vocab.label: Assisted
vocab.help: The human is the one being guided.

vocab.label: Demonstrator
vocab.help: The human's behavior is the supervision signal.

vocab.label: Collaborator
vocab.help: The human and the system act on the same task.

vocab.label: Evaluator
vocab.help: The human judges the output — user study, preference.

fields.label: What is modeled
fields.help: The physical world is objects, the bodies that touch them, and the changes that follow. This picks which of those the paper represents.

vocab.label: Object state
vocab.help: Identity, pose, parts, articulation, attributes, affordance.

vocab.label: Object change
vocab.help: The transition — what an action does to an object.

vocab.label: Agent body
vocab.help: Hands, human body, robot kinematics as physical objects.

vocab.label: Interaction
vocab.help: Contact, grasp, hand-object, human-scene.

vocab.label: Scene
vocab.help: Layout, geometry, 3D/4D reconstruction, maps.

vocab.label: Dynamics
vocab.help: Forces, materials, deformation, intuitive physics.

vocab.label: Procedure
vocab.help: Steps, goals, orderings, task graphs — time above the frame.

fields.label: Representation
fields.help: The form the world is held in. The single sharpest divider in this field: pixels vs. latents vs. explicit geometry vs. symbols.

vocab.label: Pixels
vocab.help: The state is an image or video; prediction is generation.

vocab.label: Latent
vocab.help: Prediction happens in a learned embedding — JEPA and kin.

vocab.label: 3D/4D geometry
vocab.help: Mesh, point cloud, radiance field, Gaussians, depth, 6DoF pose.

vocab.label: Language
vocab.help: State and plan are written in words; an LLM does the reasoning.

vocab.label: Graph/symbol
vocab.help: Scene graph, task graph, PDDL, automaton.

vocab.label: Program/code
vocab.help: The policy or the plan is executable code, usually written by an LLM.

vocab.label: Trajectory/flow
vocab.help: Tracks, optical flow, point flow, waypoints, action chunks.

vocab.label: Discrete tokens
vocab.help: Quantized state or action tokens in an autoregressive model.

vocab.label: Physics params
vocab.help: Explicit mass, friction, material, force — or a simulator.

fields.label: Change channel
fields.help: How the decision reaches the world. The human branch and the robot branch differ mostly here.

vocab.help: Nothing is emitted into the world.

vocab.label: Language
vocab.help: Tell the human, in words or speech.

vocab.label: Visual guidance
vocab.help: Show it: AR overlay, generated image or video, highlight.

vocab.label: Motor action
vocab.help: A policy emits joint commands, end-effector deltas, torques.

vocab.label: Plan
vocab.help: A step sequence or trajectory handed to a controller or a person.

vocab.label: Alert/intervene
vocab.help: Flag a mistake, warn, stop, ask for help.

vocab.label: Fabrication
vocab.help: The output is matter — printed, morphed, built.

fields.label: Sensing
fields.help: Where the observations come from. Egocentric and exocentric carry different information, so viewpoint changes what is learnable at all.

fields.label: Regime
fields.help: Whether the method may look at the whole clip. Online is a different problem from offline, with its own failure modes.

vocab.label: Offline
vocab.help: Full sequence available at inference.

vocab.label: Streaming
vocab.help: Causal — decides from the past only, as frames arrive.

vocab.label: Interactive
vocab.help: A person or an environment responds inside the loop.

fields.label: Horizon
fields.help: Time span the output commits to.

fields.label: Domain
fields.help: Everyday to professional is the axis that decides what a mistake costs.

vocab.label: Everyday
vocab.help: Cooking, home assembly, chores.

vocab.label: Industrial
vocab.help: Factory assembly, maintenance, inspection.

vocab.label: Clinical
vocab.help: Surgery, ultrasound, bedside care.

vocab.label: Skill/sport
vocab.help: Music, dance, sports, craft — where proficiency is the label.

vocab.label: Lab / sim
vocab.help: Benchmark tabletop, simulator, controlled rig.

vocab.label: Web-scale
vocab.help: Uncurated internet video or images.

vocab.label: Human in the loop
vocab.help: The system acts only when asked.

vocab.label: Mixed initiative
vocab.help: Both sides may start an exchange.

vocab.label: Autonomous
vocab.help: The system acts without being prompted.

fields.label: Contribution
fields.help: What the paper actually adds. A paper can be more than one.

reading_protocol.note: A paper is read in the order it is written, minus the parts that are about other papers. Introduction is a compressed abstract and related work is a map of the field, so both are skipped. What is left is the problem setting, the method, and the experiments — and each of those has a shape.

steps.name: Problem setting
steps.body: Write down the function the paper computes, at inference time, before reading how. Every input and every output gets a modality, a tensor shape, and one line on what the content actually is. Do the same for training when it differs — most of the interesting design choices hide in that difference.

steps.name: Method
steps.body: One or two sentences of intuition — the claim the architecture is an argument for. Then the components. A data engine counts as a method.

steps.name: Experiments
steps.body: Datasets and what was done to them (used as-is, re-annotated, remixed, synthesized), metrics, baselines, and one headline number. What the paper did to its data is often the real contribution.
